currentContext.business: Maruti Suzuki India Limited is engaged in the manufacture and sale of passenger and commercial vehicles, which it offers through three channels - Nexa, Arena and Commercial - and which accounted for 79.98% of turnover in FY 2025-26. It also sells aftermarket parts and accessories under the 'Maruti Suzuki Genuine Parts' and 'Maruti Suzuki Genuine Accessories' brands (15.17% of turnover). It serves a diverse customer base spanning individual consumers, government and corporate employees, and fleet and taxi operators across 28 states and 8 union territories, and exports to about 120 countries, with exports contributing 19.38% of turnover.

Manufacture of motor vehicles (NIC 2910): e VITARA (first battery electric vehicle, dedicated EV platform)
Dzire (top-selling passenger vehicle in the industry during the year)
Powertrain options offered: CNG (available in 14 out of 18 PV models; underbody CNG introduced as a segment-first)
Light commercial vehicles: LCVs sold through the Company's commercial network across multiple cities; CNG variants over 83% of segment sales in FY 2025-26 (model names not disclosed in the routed text)

currentContext.expansion: MD&A: 'Considering India's long-term growth potential and the expanding export opportunity, the Company has laid out a capacity expansion roadmap to scale production capacity to four million units per annum over the next few years.' During FY 2025-26 production ramp-up at the greenfield Kharkhoda (Haryana) facility progressed steadily, and in FY 2026-27 the Company will commission two new manufacturing plants of 250,000 units annual capacity each - one at Kharkhoda, Haryana and the other at Hansalpur, Gujarat. Planning for subsequent expansion phases continued in parallel, and all new manufacturing facilities are being designed with multi-powertrain flexibility so they can respond to future shifts in technology and customer demand; the Chairman adds that new production lines are being made flexible enough to change platforms and models as required. The Chairman's message gives the project-level detail: two lines have been commissioned at Kharkhoda with work progressing on the third; a fourth line of 250,000 capacity was commissioned at Hansalpur, 'raising installed capacity to 1 million. This is Suzuki's largest plant anywhere in the world'; work has started at a new site in Sanand, Gujarat where a total capacity of 1 million units is intended, with a proposed investment of INR 35,000 crores; and as a result of these expansion projects installed capacity 'would reach 2.9 million units at the end of FY 2026-27 and 3.65 million units at the end of FY 2030-31'. The MD&A also records that the amalgamation of Suzuki Motor Gujarat Private Limited was completed (effective 1 December 2025, appointed date 1 April 2025) and that an additional greenfield manufacturing facility in Gujarat has been announced. Beyond vehicle assembly, the BRSR lists where environment- and social-linked capex went - 'Construction of dedicated EV manufacturing facility at Hansalpur', investments in new powertrains, in-plant railway sidings at Manesar, expansion of installed renewable energy capacity and storage, digital initiatives for process optimisation and energy efficiency, infrastructure for increasing the use of renewable electricity, product safety and quality, business continuity and rainwater harvesting infrastructure - and states that 54.66% of total capex in FY 2025-26 went to such technologies versus 30.20% in FY 2024-25 (R&D: 65.88% versus 62.82%). The Chairman flags a railway siding planned at Kharkhoda on the pattern of the working Manesar siding, and Board approval to start four biogas plants in a first phase at a cost of INR 561 crores. Network build-out ran alongside plant capex: 366 sales outlets added in FY 2025-26 (868 new sales and service touchpoints taking the total to 10,527 per the Chairman), the NEXA Studio compact format scaled up, service touchpoints at 5,926, the parts distributor network expanded by a record 197 outlets to 1,574 with 51 distributor warehouses added (the highest addition in a single year), own warehouse capacity and logistics hubs significantly expanded, more than 1,500 workshops equipped for EV service, more than 300 dealer workshops on rooftop solar totalling nearly 22 MWp, and rooftop solar of 1,067 kWp commissioned at the Bengaluru and Nagpur Regional Parts Distribution Centres.
currentContext.mdna: GST reform of 22 September 2025 was the key inflection point: it improved affordability and revived small car demand, turning a 0.4% y-o-y industry decline in H1 FY 2025-26 into 16.7% growth in H2; the Company's own domestic volumes swung from -5.6% in H1 to +12.3% in H2.|Management expects that with affordability improving after GST reform, passenger vehicle demand is likely to realign more closely with India's economic growth trajectory, reversing the weakening of that relationship caused by entry-level affordability challenges.|India remains one of the most under-penetrated passenger vehicle markets globally, with long-term growth potential driven by rising incomes and increasing aspirations for personal mobility.|Growth in FY 2025-26 was constrained by production capacity rather than demand - the Company operated at nearly full capacity utilisation in H2 and ended the year with a large pending order book, which prompted acceleration of capacity expansion.|Added capacity is the near-term volume driver: 500,000 units of manufacturing capacity added in FY 2026-27, which management says will take time to ramp up fully but is expected to enable volume growth of around 10% in FY 2026-27.|First-time buyer participation rose to nearly 50% in H2 from about 42% in H1, with a large number of two-wheeler upgraders visiting showrooms - evidence of the entry-level segment reopening.|Mix: SUVs continued to account for over 56% of industry PV sales, and MSIL's own SUV contribution rose to 31% in H2 from 26% in H1 after the VICTORIS and e VITARA launches.|Powertrain mix shift towards cleaner technologies - CNG, SHEV and BEV rose to 28.9% of total industry PV sales from 24.4%; MSIL's green vehicle share reached nearly 52% of its PV sales versus about 48%.|Margin driver: operating margin (as a % of net sales) moderated to 8.4% from 10.0%, driven by adverse commodity prices and supply-side pressures from geopolitical developments, with the Company refraining from passing on the full cost increases in order to support demand recovery.|Near-term watch item: geopolitical tensions in West Asia may exert pressure on profitability through higher commodity prices, and risks related to availability of specialised materials and critical components are likely to persist.|Exports are expected to be sustained at FY 2025-26 levels despite geopolitical uncertainty, supported by a diversified footprint spanning nearly 120 countries that provides resilience against country-specific disruptions.|Non-urban demand: rural markets performed well through the year and urban markets recovered post GST reform; risks.risk: Risks associated with the increased scale of operations
risks.note: The Company aims to scale production to four million units annually by FY 2030-31, nearly double its current capacity. It took almost 40 years to reach two million units; the next two million is to be added in just 7-8 years, a pace nearly five times faster. This requires significantly more human capital, financial investment and technical know-how plus faster decision-making, and stakeholder partners - suppliers, dealers and transporters - must scale in tandem.

risks.risk: Continuity of component supplies across a concentrated supplier base
risks.note: With nearly 450 Tier-1 and about 1,500 Tier-2 suppliers, supply disruption remains a major business continuity risk. Export restrictions on certain critical materials during the year highlighted the vulnerability of globally concentrated supply chains, and geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions and logistics disruptions may continue to affect supply availability. Mitigation is localisation, alternate sources, diversified sourcing locations and the Vendor Comprehensive Excellence Programme.

risks.risk: Dependence on specialised materials and critical components sourced from a limited number of countries
risks.note: Increasing adoption of advanced automotive technologies raises dependence on specialised materials and critical components whose supply chains remain concentrated in a few countries; in an increasingly dynamic geopolitical environment, material-availability risk is likely to persist. In the near term, geopolitical tensions in West Asia may exert pressure on profitability through higher commodity prices.

risks.risk: Cost competitiveness of emerging and advanced technologies in a price-sensitive market
risks.note: Electrification, software-defined vehicles, advanced electronics and connectivity are transforming the industry, but several of these technologies are yet to reach the cost competitiveness needed for widespread adoption in a price-sensitive market such as India. As the BEV, SHEV and advanced-feature portfolio expands, holding cost competitiveness while preserving affordability is a key strategic priority, addressed through localisation, value engineering and supplier base expansion.

Sudden and significant increases in the prices of metals, energy and other commodities can adversely impact profitability and business performance, a risk reinforced by recent geopolitical developments. This risk materialised in FY 2025-26: operating margin moderated to 8.4% from 10.0%, driven by adverse commodity prices and supply-side pressures, with the Company choosing not to pass on the full cost increases. Mitigation includes consumption optimisation, alternate materials, material circularity, hedging, forward contracts and long-term commercial arrangements.

risks.risk: Capacity and capability for future readiness - skills, leadership pipeline and cultural continuity at scale
risks.note: Scaling operations amid rapid technological transformation increases demand for new skillsets both internally and across value chain partners; at the same time, sustaining the organisational values, culture of partnership and continuous-improvement spirit built over four decades becomes harder as scale and workforce expand.

risks.risk: Cybersecurity, including cyber risk in the supply chain
risks.note: Cyber threats are growing and the Company protects information assets through employee education on phishing and proactive monitoring. It has created a cybersecurity assessment framework based on global standards for suppliers, and over 400 Tier-1 supplier partners have been assessed so far, on the view that supply-chain cyber resilience is a business-continuity issue.

risks.risk: Foreign exchange exposure on imports and exports
risks.note: The Company is exposed to fluctuations in foreign exchange rates, mainly on the import of components, raw materials and services and on the export of vehicles and services. It runs a structured exchange risk management policy and uses hedge instruments judiciously depending on market conditions and the currency view. The MD&A separately records a sharp depreciation of the rupee against the US dollar towards the end of the year.

one-line thesis: Maruti Suzuki is redefining its market leadership by aggressively expanding its high-margin SUV portfolio with cutting-edge hybrid technology, leveraging Toyota's manufacturing partnership to accelerate electrification while navigating persistent semiconductor shortages and commodity inflation through strategic pricing and cost controls.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: India's largest passenger vehicle manufacturer, making and selling passenger and commercial vehicles through its Nexa, Arena and Commercial channels, supported by parent Suzuki Motor Corporation.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Maruti Suzuki India Limited is engaged in the manufacture and sale of passenger and commercial vehicles, which it offers through three channels - Nexa, Arena and Commercial - and which accounted for 79.98% of turnover in FY 2025-26. It also sells aftermarket parts and accessories under the 'Maruti Suzuki Genuine Parts' and 'Maruti Suzuki Genuine Accessories' brands (15.17% of turnover). It serves a diverse customer base spanning individual consumers, government and corporate employees, and fleet and taxi operators across 28 states and 8 union territories, and exports to about 120 countries, with exports contributing 19.38% of turnover.

group_structure.body:
- Suzuki Motor Corporation (SMC) — related party: Holding body corporate / parent. Form AOC-2 discloses long-term contracts with recurring transactions for both purchase of goods and services from SMC and sale of goods and services to SMC, for April 2025 - March 2026, stated to be in the ordinary course of business and at arm's length.
- Suzuki Motor Gujarat Private Limited (SMG) — subsidiary: Former wholly owned material subsidiary (Hansalpur). Scheme of Amalgamation with MSIL approved by NCLT New Delhi on 6th November 2025, effective 1st December 2025 with an appointed date of 1st April 2025; SMG ceased to be a subsidiary w.e.f. 1st December 2025. demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- GST reform of 22 September 2025 was the key inflection point: it improved affordability and revived small car demand, turning a 0.4% y-o-y industry decline in H1 FY 2025-26 into 16.7% growth in H2; the Company's own domestic volumes swung from -5.6% in H1 to +12.3% in H2.
- Management expects that with affordability improving after GST reform, passenger vehicle demand is likely to realign more closely with India's economic growth trajectory, reversing the weakening of that relationship caused by entry-level affordability challenges.
- India remains one of the most under-penetrated passenger vehicle markets globally, with long-term growth potential driven by rising incomes and increasing aspirations for personal mobility.
- Growth in FY 2025-26 was constrained by production capacity rather than demand - the Company operated at nearly full capacity utilisation in H2 and ended the year with a large pending order book, which prompted acceleration of capacity expansion.
- Added capacity is the near-term volume driver: 500,000 units of manufacturing capacity added in FY 2026-27, which management says will take time to ramp up fully but is expected to enable volume growth of around 10% in FY 2026-27.
- First-time buyer participation rose to nearly 50% in H2 from about 42% in H1, with a large number of two-wheeler upgraders visiting showrooms - evidence of the entry-level segment reopening.
- Mix: SUVs continued to account for over 56% of industry PV sales, and MSIL's own SUV contribution rose to 31% in H2 from 26% in H1 after the VICTORIS and e VITARA launches.
- Powertrain mix shift towards cleaner technologies - CNG, SHEV and BEV rose to 28.9% of total industry PV sales from 24.4%; MSIL's green vehicle share reached nearly 52% of its PV sales versus about 48%.
- Margin driver: operating margin (as a % of net sales) moderated to 8.4% from 10.0%, driven by adverse commodity prices and supply-side pressures from geopolitical developments, with the Company refraining from passing on the full cost increases in order to support demand recovery.
- Near-term watch item: geopolitical tensions in West Asia may exert pressure on profitability through higher commodity prices, and risks related to availability of specialised materials and critical components are likely to persist.
- Exports are expected to be sustained at FY 2025-26 levels despite geopolitical uncertainty, supported by a diversified footprint spanning nearly 120 countries that provides resilience against country-specific disruptions.
- Non-urban demand: rural markets performed well through the year and urban markets recovered post GST reform; non-urban markets now contribute over 52% of sales versus about 48% previously.
- Chairman's market view: the car industry is estimated to grow to 6.1 to 6.3 million units by FY 2030-31, with the small car market share growing significantly faster than in the last five years, which could lead to changes in the Company's longer-term targets.
- At the end of FY 2025-26 the Company had around 190,000 pending customer orders, of which nearly 130,000 were in the small car segment, highlighting the strength of underlying demand.
- Chairman's message: 'We ended March with 1.9 lakh pending bookings, a result of inadequate manufacturing capacity of the models in demand.'
- Dealer inventory remained low at around 12 days of stock, reflecting continued strong retail demand since the GST reform.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: MD&A: 'Considering India's long-term growth potential and the expanding export opportunity, the Company has laid out a capacity expansion roadmap to scale production capacity to four million units per annum over the next few years.' During FY 2025-26 production ramp-up at the greenfield Kharkhoda (Haryana) facility progressed steadily, and in FY 2026-27 the Company will commission two new manufacturing plants of 250,000 units annual capacity each - one at Kharkhoda, Haryana and the other at Hansalpur, Gujarat. Planning for subsequent expansion phases continued in parallel, and all new manufacturing facilities are being designed with multi-powertrain flexibility so they can respond to future shifts in technology and customer demand; the Chairman adds that new production lines are being made flexible enough to change platforms and models as required. The Chairman's message gives the project-level detail: two lines have been commissioned at Kharkhoda with work progressing on the third; a fourth line of 250,000 capacity was commissioned at Hansalpur, 'raising installed capacity to 1 million. This is Suzuki's largest plant anywhere in the world'; work has started at a new site in Sanand, Gujarat where a total capacity of 1 million units is intended, with a proposed investment of INR 35,000 crores; and as a result of these expansion projects installed capacity 'would reach 2.9 million units at the end of FY 2026-27 and 3.65 million units at the end of FY 2030-31'. The MD&A also records that the amalgamation of Suzuki Motor Gujarat Private Limited was completed (effective 1 December 2025, appointed date 1 April 2025) and that an additional greenfield manufacturing facility in Gujarat has been announced. Beyond vehicle assembly, the BRSR lists where environment- and social-linked capex went - 'Construction of dedicated EV manufacturing facility at Hansalpur', investments in new powertrains, in-plant railway sidings at Manesar, expansion of installed renewable energy capacity and storage, digital initiatives for process optimisation and energy efficiency, infrastructure for increasing the use of renewable electricity, product safety and quality, business continuity and rainwater harvesting infrastructure - and states that 54.66% of total capex in FY 2025-26 went to such technologies versus 30.20% in FY 2024-25 (R&D: 65.88% versus 62.82%). The Chairman flags a railway siding planned at Kharkhoda on the pattern of the working Manesar siding, and Board approval to start four biogas plants in a first phase at a cost of INR 561 crores. Network build-out ran alongside plant capex: 366 sales outlets added in FY 2025-26 (868 new sales and service touchpoints taking the total to 10,527 per the Chairman), the NEXA Studio compact format scaled up, service touchpoints at 5,926, the parts distributor network expanded by a record 197 outlets to 1,574 with 51 distributor warehouses added (the highest addition in a single year), own warehouse capacity and logistics hubs significantly expanded, more than 1,500 workshops equipped for EV service, more than 300 dealer workshops on rooftop solar totalling nearly 22 MWp, and rooftop solar of 1,067 kWp commissioned at the Bengaluru and Nagpur Regional Parts Distribution Centres.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, bullish, and proactive; strong emphasis on product-led growth, technology leadership (hybrid), and long-term decarbonization; dismissive of short-term OPEX noise; assertive on market share capture; transparent on constraints (supply chain, costs)

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Scale and share: India's largest passenger vehicle manufacturer, with a retail market share of about 40% in FY 2025-26 and a leadership position across almost all product segments; six of the top ten best-selling cars in the industry were from Maruti Suzuki
- Parent technology access: the Company 'offers relevant products and technology that Indian customers need by leveraging the unique ability of Suzuki Motor Corporation to design feature-rich, safer, environment-friendly products with world class quality at an affordable price'
- Export franchise built on the parent's network: export volumes of 447,774 units in FY 2025-26 across over 120 markets; nearly 50% of all passenger vehicles exported from India; India's leading PV exporter for the fifth consecutive year
- Distribution reach, especially non-urban: 366 sales outlets added in FY 2025-26, over 2,900 outlets in non-urban markets, and 868 new sales and service touchpoints taking the total to 10,527 (Chairman's message)
- Service and aftermarket network as a switching-cost moat: 5,926 service touchpoints, 1,574 parts distribution sales outlets, more than 95,500 unique parts and accessories, and over 50,000 independent workshops connected through Parts Kart
- CNG leadership: CNG options in 14 of 18 PV models and nearly 70% market share in that segment, with CNG PV sales up 19.7% y-o-y
- Multi-powertrain portfolio (CNG, mild hybrid, strong hybrid, BEV) taking green vehicles to nearly 52% of total PV sales in FY 2025-26 from about 48% the previous year
- Safety differentiation: six airbags and Electronic Stability Control standard on nearly 100% of the portfolio - 'the only OEM in the country to offer such safety features as standard across a wide and diverse portfolio'
- Supplier ecosystem and localisation: nearly 450 Tier-1 and about 1,500 Tier-2 suppliers, with localisation described as a key pillar of long-term supply chain resilience
- Digitalisation of the purchase journey: 24 of 26 customer interaction points digitalised, and over 39% of customers sourcing finance through Maruti Suzuki Smart Finance
